newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton mixed as Gujarat up, Punjab ranged.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton mixed as Gujarat up, Punjab ranged.

text.p: Gujarat cotton climbed up but Punjab varieties remained steady in a narrow price band on the local market, dealers said.
Gujarat varieties rose on reports that the state government had stepped up direct purchases from farmers ahead of some local assembly elections.

"Gujarat government plans to attract more votes of farmers by doing so," one dealer said. In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) moved up 300 rupees to 13,000/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) and Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose 400/500 rupees at 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy.

Punjab cotton was quiet in a narrow price band amid limited activity. Punjab saw-ginned was quoted at 1,500/1,650 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab F-414 was quiet at 1,880/1,900 rupees and Bengal-deshi at 870/920 rupees per maund.
The Bombay cotton market will be closed on Friday, which is Good Friday.
